assessment.reason: Price clears break-even on model numbers, but two Washington defensemen are listed out. That could push Chychrun into a larger offensive role than the shrunk assist rate assumes.

blocking_checks: Whether Chychrun runs the top power-play unit with Sandin out. Heavier power-play usage would raise his assist chances and could erase the under's cushion.

qualitative_review.countercase: With two defensemen out, Chychrun may absorb power-play and offensive-zone minutes. Montréal is on a back-to-back with a projected goalie. A higher assist rate than the shrunk estimate would quickly bring fair odds toward -120.

assessment.reason: The under leans on a prior-heavy projection from six appearances. Several Colorado absences could change Hughes's deployment before the 8:40 PM EDT puck drop.
assessment.model_case: Projected 0.38 points against a 0.5 line on 14.9 minutes. With only six appearances, position priors and shrinkage drive most of the estimate. A role change would quickly undercut it.
assessment.price_case: Main line at -130. Model fair odds are about -215 and minimum about -181. Market odds sit near break-even, and the blend leaves a thin margin. Two other books quote it.
assessment.context_case: Makar and Merkulov listings could reshape Colorado's lines and power play. Neither listing mentions Hughes, and his role is unverified. Dallas is also depleted and plays a back-to-back with an unconfirmed goalie.
blocking_checks: Hughes's line and power-play assignment given Colorado's absences. A top-six or power-play promotion would raise his point odds beyond what the prior-heavy model assumes.

qualitative_review.countercase: Colorado is missing forwards, and Makar's status is unresolved, which could elevate Hughes's minutes. Dallas is thin at center and on a back-to-back, which could tilt play toward Colorado. The small sample makes the projection fragile.

evidence.interpretation: If Makar sits, Colorado's scoring rate may dip, which favors the under. But power-play roles could shift unpredictably.

assessment.reason: The under clears break-even across the supplied sensitivity band. However, the projected mean sits above the 1.5 line, and a Washington center's game-day status could shift Strome's minutes upward. That would cut against the under.
assessment.model_case: The projected mean of about 1.65 shots is above the line, so the under relies on low-count variance at 16.7 projected minutes. Line and power-play assignment are unverified. Added minutes or power-play time would push the mean higher and erode the case.
assessment.price_case: At +130 on the main line, break-even is roughly 43 in 100. The model's low sensitivity case still clears that, but the blended view leaves only a thin margin. Three other books price the under shorter, so this is a single-book outlier rather than consensus support.
assessment.context_case: Dubois is listed through game day, and Montréal is missing a defenseman. Both point, if anything, toward more Strome shots. The listing snapshot is not lineup confirmation, and Strome's own role is unverified.
blocking_checks: Whether Dubois plays. His absence could raise Strome's even-strength and power-play minutes and push the shot mean further above 1.5.

qualitative_review.countercase: A projected mean above the line plus a possible center absence on Washington's side could expand Strome's usage. Montréal's thin defense and a back-to-back goalie could also inflate shot volume. Together, these would make the market's shorter under price look correct.
open_checks: Confirm Strome's line and power-play unit at morning skate or warmups.
Reconfirm the +130 price and line before deciding.
Check whether Washington's back-to-back affects Strome's minutes.

evidence.interpretation: If Dubois sits, Strome may absorb extra center minutes or power-play time, which would weaken the under. If Dubois returns, the projected role is more likely to hold.

findings.note: NHL.com's projected lineup for the Oct. 13 game, the first half of this home-and-home with Dallas, has Hughes on the third line with Jaden Schwartz and Fedor Svechkov, not with Colorado's top-six scorers.

The Oct. 9 RotoWire note says Hughes got his first NHL point in his fourth game, with 11 shots, in a third-line role that also gets power-play time. The page also says it's unclear whether an Avalanche defenseman, apparently Makar, will play Wednesday's rematch.

Dated Sept. 30. The team said Hughes was set for Colorado's top power-play unit with MacKinnon, Landeskog, Necas and Makar, which gives him a real path to a point. He had a preseason hat trick and 14 points in 17 AHL playoff games.

Old 2025-26 Rotowire notes, not news on tonight's game: Strome had 139 shots in 77 games (about 1.8 per game, slightly above the 1.5 line) and had dropped off the top line at times during a slump. Search found no current injury, lineup, projection or pick for Oct 14.
